thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @emma (on-call) — high p99 across streaming endpoints in eu-west-2, observed starting 2026-03-15T09:44:30Z. Auto-alert: p99 spike > 2.5s for >5m.

emma: got it, I'm oncall. checking dashboards now. which customers?

raj: I see p95 ~ 900ms but p99 jumping to 3.2s, streaming tail stalls visible. top traces show TLS handshake retries + DNS timeouts to nat-egress workers.

marta: seeing packet loss counters bump in azb -> azc cross-zone path, retransmits and SYN retries.

leo: service mesh logs show intermittent 503s from forward-proxy in eu-west-2c. connection resets correlate with NAT port exhaustion hints.

ben: customer-facing: a few active customers reported partial streaming hitches; no full request failures but tail latency affects client streaming timeouts.

emma: severity? should we page platform team and start handoff?

incident-bot: Current severity: Sev2 (customer impact but partial). Recommended: escalate to eng-networking and open a mitigation channel.

emma: @raj @marta @leo — pls join. I'm going to run tcpdump on NAT gateway and check conntrack.

raj: running: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 'port 443 and (tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0)' -c 200`

marta: copying packet capture to /tmp/nat-sample.pcap. early look: lots of SYN retransmits and TLS handshake timeouts to upstream model-proxy pods. some DNS NXDOMAINs when contacting internal resolver.

leo: curling model endpoint from inside cluster shows occasional `TLS handshake timeout` and `no route to host` for affected AZs.

infra-bot: Quick check: NAT ephemeral ports used 86% in eu-west-2c, 41% in eu-west-2a, 37% in eu-west-2b. Route table shows uneven distribution from service placement.

emma: aha — ephemeral port pressure in 2c. possible storm of short-lived connections from streaming clients + backend SDK reconnects. Can we shift egress for canary traffic?

raj: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) widen NAT ephemeral port range on 2c, 2) enable connection pooling at forward-proxy, 3) failover subset of traffic to eu-west-2a for routing.

marta: DNS flapping also suspicious — internal resolver shows increased latencies ~150-400ms. Could be cross-zone DNS queries hitting overloaded resolver in 2c.

emma: let's do quick traffic steering: add a routing policy to prefer 2a/2b for new sessions, keep existing connections. roll change, monitor.

ben: tagging affected customers and sending proactive note: "We are investigating intermittent streaming hitches in eu-west-2; engineering is mitigating; no data loss confirmed."

sophia: I'll prepare status update for infra-alerts channel.

raj: executing routing change: `rbctl set-policy egress-preference eu-west-2 prefer [2a,2b] --dry-run=false`

infra-bot: Route preference applied. BGP path updates propagated in ~12s. New sessions now 78% to 2a/2b.

marta: post-change metrics: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s in 90s. packet loss counters in 2c stopping climbing. DNS latency trending down.

emma: great. continue monitoring for 15m. rolling mitigation worked.

leo: need durable fix: either increase NAT capacity in 2c (add more ENIs / scale NAT instances) or reduce total ephemeral usage by connection reuse.

raj: short-term: queue change to increase ephemeral ports + bump NAT service count in 2c. medium-term: implement long-lived proxy connections between model-proxy and egress to reduce churn.

ben: customers: some reported improved behavior after ~2 minutes, others still seeing delayed chunks. escalate to account teams for top 5 customers.

emma: timeline note for incident doc:
- 09:44:30 alert triggered (p99 >2.5s)
- 09:45:10 on-call ack + initial triage
- 09:47:05 identified NAT ephemeral pressure in eu-west-2c + DNS latency
- 09:48:40 applied egress routing preference to 2a/2b
- 09:50:30 p99 reduced to ~1.1s, customer reports improving

marta: logs sample (scrubbed):
```
[09:46:12] proxy.go: connection reset by peer during TLS handshake
[09:46:15] nat.go: conntrack lookup failed: table full
[09:46:19] resolver.go: DNS query timeout -> 200ms retry
```

leo: any risk with the routing change? did we create new hot-spot?

emma: infra-bot shows balanced usage now: 2a/2b up by ~25% but within capacity. keep watch.

raj: also observed streaming stalls at tail due to retransmit bursts; adding short-term TCP keepalive tuning to proxy to reduce half-open churn.

sophia: started incident thread in status page and added note: "Mitigation applied; monitoring. Postmortem pending."

ben: recommend customer-facing post: short explanation + apology + ETA for full root cause and fix.

emma: assigning actions: @raj increase NAT capacity in 2c (P0 change), @marta validate DNS resolver health & add fallback resolver, @leo include connection pooling proposal in next sprint, @sophia draft external comms. I'll run the incident timeline and start a postmortem doc.

raj: running scale: `infra-scale nat-gw eu-west-2c +2` -> submitted, in progress.

infra-bot: scale job completed in 3m. ephemeral ports reduced to 32% usage in 2c.

marta: DNS fallback added to resolvers config to prefer healthy resolver in other AZs. Config pushed.

emma: monitoring 30m window. if stable, we'll close incident with follow-up tasks. great work, team. :thumbsup:

ben: capture customer examples and latency traces for postmortem.

emma: closing notes: impact limited to streaming tail latency (p99 breach), mitigation via egress steering + NAT scale + DNS fallback. No evidence of data loss, customer retries caused longer streams. next steps: postmortem, instrument connection churn, long-lived proxy work, NAT capacity planning.

incident-bot: Incident marked "Mitigated" at 2026-03-15T10:08:30Z. Postmortem owner: emma.

sophia: I'll schedule a 30m blameless postmortem review for tomorrow.

emma: thanks all.
